newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM sees stronger German emphasis on euro.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM sees stronger German emphasis on euro.

text.p: Germany is becoming increasingly aware that it risks being hit hardest if the European single currency does not go ahead as planned, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Saturday.
He was speaking on Belgian television about this week's summit of European Union leaders in Amsterdam, which put the single currency, the euro, back on track for its launch in January 1, 1999.

"What struck me the most...is that German political and economic leaders have started to realise that if, by misfortune, the euro did not materialise, it is the D-mark and Germany that would bear the full brunt, and that would risk plunging them into an economic crisis," Dehaene told French-language RTBF television.

"It's the first time I hear German officials saying something apart from 'we want to keep our strong mark', and instead that the euro must absolutely work because the mark is maybe a bit too strong compared with what the economic community wants," Dehaene added.

EU leaders gave their final blessing in Amsterdam to a stability pact for the single currency after the French government won a series of comitments that the 15-nation bloc would work more closely to fight unemployment.
